content.title: About
content.content: Brandy Alexander is a classic cocktail made of brandy, dark crème de cacao and cream. It is usually served in a cocktail glass and garnished with grated nutmeg. The flavor combines the sweetness of cream, the bitterness of chocolate and the aroma of brandy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink was created in the early 1920s and named after Russian Emperor Alexander III.
The original recipe used cognac, later replaced by generic brandy.
Brandy Alexander appears frequently in literature and film, for example in the movie “Casablanca”.
Grated nutmeg used for garnish gives the drink its distinctive aroma.
Variations include substituting ice cream for cream or adding vanilla syrup.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Dark crème de cacao provides flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of vitamin B2
items.content: Brandy, like other spirits, contains small amounts of riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate consumption can be relaxing
items.content: Alcohol in modest amounts has a calming effect on the nervous system.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Brandy Alexander contains alcohol, so it is not recommended for pregnant women, children, or people with liver problems.

items.title: High calorie count
items.content: Cream and sugar make the cocktail calorie‑dense; moderation is important for weight management.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should replace cream with a plant‑based alternative.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve the cocktail chilled in a cocktail glass, garnished with grated nutmeg. It can be enjoyed as a dessert drink after dinner or as a festive toast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Ingredients (brandy, crème de cacao, cream) should be stored separately: brandy and crème de cacao in a cool, dark place; cream in the refrigerator and used within a few days after opening.

content.title: About
content.content: Hush Puppy is a brand of comfortable footwear known for its soft, breathable materials and easy‑going fit. The shoes are suitable for everyday wear, travel, and an active lifestyle.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The brand was founded in 1958 in the United States and quickly gained popularity thanks to its innovative EVA rubber sole.
Hush Puppy shoes are often called “travel shoes” because they fold easily and require little break‑in time.
The “Original” model has sold over 30 million pairs worldwide.
In the 1970s, Hush Puppy introduced the first mass‑market shoe with an anatomical footbed.
The brand supports eco‑friendly initiatives, using recycled materials in several collections.

items.title: Comfort and foot support
items.content: A soft sole and anatomical footbed reduce joint stress and help prevent foot fatigue.

items.title: Breathable materials
items.content: Mesh uppers provide good ventilation, decreasing sweat and the risk of fungal infections.

items.title: Lightweight
items.content: The shoes weigh considerably less than traditional models, lessening load during long periods of standing.

items.title: Impact absorption
items.content: Flexible soles cushion impacts, protecting the foot from shock.

items.title: Versatility
items.content: Suitable for casual walks as well as light physical activity, making them practical in many situations.

items.title: Improper sizing
items.content: Shoes that are too loose or too tight can cause blisters, pressure points, and discomfort.

items.title: Limited support for extreme activities
items.content: For intense sports training, the shoes may not provide enough stabilization.

items.title: Material allergies
items.content: Some users may be sensitive to synthetic materials used in the upper or footbed.

items.title: Sole wear
items.content: With prolonged use the sole can lose its cushioning, reducing overall comfort.

content.title: How to Wear
content.content: Hush Puppy shoes pair well with jeans, shorts, lightweight trousers, or athleisure outfits. Wearing cotton socks is recommended for optimal breathability.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the shoes in a dry, well‑ventilated place away from direct sunlight. For long‑term storage, keep them in a box or bag to maintain their shape.

content.title: About
content.content: Cooked onions are peeled onion bulbs that have been boiled until tender. Heat softens the texture, reduces sharpness and brings out a natural sweetness. They are a common ingredient in soups, sauces, stews and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions belong to the Amaryllidaceae family and are close relatives of garlic, shallots and leeks.
Cooking destroys many of the volatile compounds that cause tears when cutting raw onions.
Cooked onions are featured in classic dishes worldwide, such as French onion soup, Indian pakoras and Japanese nikujaga.
Heat converts some of the onion’s sugars, making the flavor sweeter.
When stored in an airtight container, cooked onions keep in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cooked onions retain quercetin and sulfur compounds that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Sulfur compounds may help lower cholesterol and improve blood vessel function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Although some vitamin C is lost during heating, cooked onions still provide a modest amount of this immune‑supporting vitamin.

items.title: May aid blood‑sugar regulation
items.content: Phytochemicals in onions can improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Promotes digestive health
items.content: The fiber in onions supports regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, ranging from skin itching to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Onions contain fructans, which can cause gas and bloating in sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: If cooked in salted water, the added sodium should be considered in the overall diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add cooked onions to soups, sauces, purees, salads, casseroles and pie fillings. They also make a tasty topping for meat or fish. For extra flavor, briefly sauté the cooked onions before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool cooked onions to room temperature, then place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – they retain quality for about 3 months.

rice-white-with-lentils-fat-added.title: White Rice with Lentils and Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice with lentils and added fat is a ready‑to‑eat product that combines boiled white rice, cooked lentils, and vegetable fats. It provides the carbohydrates of rice, plant protein from lentils, and the energy density of fats, making it a convenient meal for quick nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rice‑lentil combination is traditional in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines.
Lentils are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown for over 8,000 years.
Added vegetable fats improve absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
The dish is often used in sports nutrition because of its high calorie and protein content.
The white rice is polished, reducing fiber but making it softer and faster to digest.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and fats provides a quick and sustained energy boost, useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Lentils supply plant‑based protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Lentils are a good source of iron and folic acid, essential for blood formation and metabolism.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Vegetable fats, especially monounsaturated fatty acids, may help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Boiled rice and soft lentils are gentle on the stomach, suitable for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added fats increase the calorie count, so portion control is important for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Possible gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: While rice and lentils are naturally gluten‑free, processing equipment may be shared with gluten‑containing foods.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to lentils.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: If the product is seasoned, monitor sodium intake, especially for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be served as a standalone meal, added to salads, used as a side dish for meat or fish, or reheated in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For long‑term storage (over 6 months) keep refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
